# Top 57 Remote Patient Monitoring startups

Updated: Jun 23, 2026

\|

By [Jason Kwon](https://www.medicalstartups.org/top/remote-patient-monitoring/#author)

Like


20

These startups develop wearable sensors, mobile health apps and connected medical devices that enable real-time data collection and remote patient monitoring.

1

[Biofourmis](https://www.medicalstartups.org/startup/biofourmis/)

[![Biofourmis](https://www.medicalstartups.org/pics/startups/b/Biofourmis.jpg)](https://www.medicalstartups.org/startup/biofourmis/)

Country: **Singapore** \| Funding: **$463.6M**

Biofourmis is reinventing remote patient monitoring by detecting personalized patterns predictive of patient’s health deterioration

2

[Huma](https://www.medicalstartups.org/startup/huma/)

[![Huma](https://www.medicalstartups.org/pics/startups/h/Huma.jpg)](https://www.medicalstartups.org/startup/huma/)

Country: **UK** \| Funding: **$322.6M**

Huma offers a health platform used for remote patient monitoring and biological data gathering for preventative healthcare.

3

[Cadence](https://www.medicalstartups.org/startup/cadence/)

[![Cadence](https://www.medicalstartups.org/pics/startups/c/Cadence.jpg)](https://www.medicalstartups.org/startup/cadence/)

Country: **USA** \| Funding: **$241M**

Cadence offers a clinical intelligent remote patient monitoring platform for chronic care management for older adults. Its AI-powered Proactive Care Engine analyzes data in real time, alerts clinical teams to emerging health risks between visits, and supports patients in receiving medication adjustments and lifestyle guidance. The company's supervised AI agents monitor patient vital signs daily. The platform is integrated into health systems' medical groups, clinical workflows and electronic medical records.

4

[Fire1](https://www.medicalstartups.org/startup/fire1/)

[![Fire1](https://www.medicalstartups.org/pics/startups/f/Fire1.jpg)](https://www.medicalstartups.org/startup/fire1/)

Country: **Ireland** \| Funding: **$202.1M**

FIRE1 offers an implant that allows for remote monitoring of patients with heart failure.

5

[Lark](https://www.medicalstartups.org/startup/lark/)

[![Lark](https://www.medicalstartups.org/pics/startups/l/Lark.jpg)](https://www.medicalstartups.org/startup/lark/)

Country: **USA** \| Funding: **$195.7M**

6

Country: **Scotland** \| Funding: **$93.2M**

Snap40 develops a device that monitors users via its single medical-grade wearable device, worn on the upper arm. This includes relative changes in systolic blood pressure, respiratory rate, heart rate, mobility, blood oxygen saturation, and temperature, as well as perspiration and movement levels.

Editor: **Jason Kwon**

Jason Kwon is a senior editor for MedicalStartups. He has previously covered the pharmaceutical and medical research industries for FDAnews and worked as a head of marketing for medical startup Sonic Therapeutics. Before that, he co-founded a startup consulting business for emerging entrepreneurial hubs in Asia. Jason graduated from St. Bonaventure University’s journalism school. In his free time, Jason enjoys yoga, watching movie trailers, traveling to places where he can't get cell service. You can contact Jason at jaskwon(at)medicalstartups(dot)com
